hook.text: Three contractors bid $50M, $55M, and $42M. The lowest price isn't always the best choice.

buildup.text: Competitive bidding invites contractors to submit sealed prices — lowest responsive bid wins.

discovery.text: Prequalification screens bidders for experience, financial strength, and safety records.

twist.text: Abnormally low bids often lead to disputes, change orders, and project failures.

climax.text: Best-value procurement weighs qualifications and price together — not just the lowest number.

punchline.text: The cheapest bid builds the cheapest building. Value matters more than price.

quiz.question: Why can the lowest construction bid be problematic?
options: Low bidders always use higher-quality materials to compensate
Abnormally low bids often lead to disputes, change orders, and project failures
Low bids are always fraudulent and violate procurement laws

details.summary: Construction bidding is the competitive process where contractors submit price proposals to perform work defined by drawings and specifications. Procurement encompasses the entire process of selecting contractors and suppliers, including prequalification, invitation to bid, bid evaluation.
details.whyItMatters: Effective procurement ensures qualified contractors compete fairly, producing the best value for the owner. Poor procurement leads to unqualified bidders, disputes, and project failures.
takeaways: Prequalification screens contractors for financial capacity and experience
Competitive bidding on equal terms ensures fair pricing and accountability
Best-value selection balances price with qualifications and technical approach

faq.question: Should the lowest bidder always win the construction contract?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Lowest-bid selection can attract unqualified contractors who underbid to win work, then seek profit through change orders and claims. Best-value procurement evaluates qualifications, past performance, safety record, and technical approach alongside price.

faq.question: What does prequalification of contractors involve?
faq.answer: Prequalification evaluates a contractor's financial stability through bonding capacity and financial statements, relevant experience on similar projects, safety record including EMR ratings, available equipment and staffing, and references from previous clients.
